title: Mandate 82: every agent pulls and merges origin/main every 10 minutes
goal: Vision: V-7. CEO directive 2026-11-16: "Make a mandate that every agent must merge and pull every 10 minutes". Record it as CEO Mandate 82: the constitution entry, docs/ceo-mandate-82.md, the AGENTS.md section and table row, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md, the README list and the self-build contract, each guarded by the governance tests. The measuring and refusing lives in the workflow tool, in the commercial repository (its T-CLAUDEMANDATE82-1).

reuse.searched: Both repositories' rules on staying current: Mandate 74 clause 3 (latest remote before starting, when resuming and before every commit; commit refused more than 20 commits behind), Mandate 80 (review ready work for integration every ten minutes), AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, README.md, docs/ceo-mandate-74..81.md, .agents/identity.json, the self-build contract (crates/susi-core/src/self_build.rs) and the governance guards (tests/architecture_tests.rs, tests/agent_bootstrap.rs, tests/three_pillars_governance.rs). The workflow tool that measures and refuses (susi-dev-workflow freshness, commit guard, workflow fresh/check/sync) lives in intellibitz/susi-commercial-apps and is extended there, not rebuilt here. The new mandate follows the layout of Mandates 76 to 81; no new code path, dependency or harvest in core.

limitations: Core carries the rule, its documents, the self-build contract clause and the governance tests. The measuring and refusing is in the workflow tool in intellibitz/susi-commercial-apps (its T-CLAUDEMANDATE82-1); core's commit hooks run that tool when it is installed.

Nothing wakes an agent at ten minutes: an agent that neither commits nor runs the tool is not timed. A tool built before the commercial change enforces only the 20-commit limit until the host rebuilds it from main.
CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md name the workflow tool for the pull, not the plain Git command, because tests/agent_bootstrap.rs keeps retired bootstrap commands out of those pointer files.
Main is unqualified development, not a release.
